summary.intent: Plan and then execute GSD Phase 69 of CipherBox — porting the node/v3 data model to the Rust desktop stack (FUSE on Unix, WinFsp on Windows) and making clients grant-root-aware, mirroring the TS Phase 68.2 SDK-owned read chain — running end-to-end from planning through parallel worktree-isolated execution.
summary.outcome: Planning completed (18 plans across research/validation/patterns/plan-checker gates, recovering from a mid-run planner crash). Execution merged the full crates/core + crates/sdk foundation (13/18 plans: Node codec/seal, gated read-chain, rotation engine with CRIT-1/HIGH-3/HIGH-4/ROT-06, floor gate, grant-scope predicate, write-plane emit API, write-owner materialization) after three successive architectural blockers were discovered and resolved via re-scoping. The final atomic FUSE consumer flip (69-09) proved too large for one-shot execution and is mid-grind via a bounded slice runbook (Slice 1: InodeKind reshape, Slice 2: read materialization landed; Slices 3-5 plus 69-10/69-13/69-14 remain).

repo: The FUSE mount is a read-WRITE vault owner (signs IPNS records, seals children under parent keys) — unlike the TS web 68.2 mirror which is read-only; InodeKind must carry ipns_private_key/write_key, not just read_key.
D-07 dual-keying: SealedChildRef (read plane) keyed by ipnsName, WriteChildRef (write plane) keyed by childId UUID — pairing must be by published.id/child_id, never ipnsName.

crates/fuse feature-gating: default=["fuse"], platform/windows/* is behind cfg(feature="winfsp") and excluded from default `cargo check --workspace` (only checked under --features winfsp in cargo-windows CI).
list_folder_owned rejects file nodes (NotAFolder) — file-node content reads need a separate sanctioned SC#6 gated fetch entrypoint (planned as a Slice 5 task).
NodeContent.file_iv must be hex-encoded (content_ops.rs does hex::decode) to match the legacy iv_hex read path.

ApiNodeFetcher is a borrow adapter (`struct ApiNodeFetcher<'a> { api: &'a ApiClient }`) with no ::new — must be constructed inline at each call site, not stored as a struct field (storing it beside owned Arc<ApiClient> would be self-referential).

WriteQueue.journal_dir is pub(crate) and unreachable from the fuse crate — high_water must be derived from the local journal_dir captured before it's moved into WriteQueue::new, not read back off journal.

The originally-cited cross-crate 'JournalOp weld' (parent_metadata: FolderMetadata in crates/sdk/src/queue.rs) was stale/nonexistent — that field actually lives in fuse-side MkdirJournalResult (journal_helpers.rs:97), not the cross-crate JournalOp enum.

Blast radius of the legacy crypto model in crates/fuse is large: ~232 folder_key refs, ~204 ipns_private_key refs, 15 ecies::unwrap_key sites, ~12,300 LOC across inode.rs/replay.rs/metadata.rs/journal_helpers.rs/write_ops — a >1000-site single-shot migration with no compiling sub-unit.

code.finding: ResolvedChild carries no key material ({ipns_name, name, kind, size, modified_at, sequence}) — read-only listing projection.
resolve_child unseals the child read-key and immediately zeroizes it — never touches the write-body.
list_folder_owned entrypoint (added in 69-17) recovers per-node {read_key, write_key, ipns_private_key} through the same SC#6 gate as list_folder.

InodeKind enum reshaped in Slice 1 to Root/Folder/File variants each carrying read_key, write_key, ipns_private_key (all Zeroizing, non-Option) — dropped legacy encrypted_folder_key/folder_key/file_meta_ipns_name/versions fields.
MkdirJournalResult struct holds parent_metadata: FolderMetadata — this is the real (fuse-local) location of the field the research mistakenly attributed to crates/sdk/src/queue.rs.

seal_published_node(node, read_key, write_key, write_body) added in 69-15 to seal both the read-body and write-body of a PublishedNode (previously only the read-body was sealed; write_sealed was never populated).

workflow: For a crashed planner mid-run, the filesystem-fallback recovery is to spawn a fresh single-plan planner for just the missing plan rather than restart the whole planning pass; then re-verify frontmatter/requirements coverage.
The GSD commit helper has a recurring false-negative reporting 'commit_failed' even when the commit lands cleanly — always verify via `git log --oneline -1`, never blindly retry.

Worktree executors sometimes mis-report `expected_base` as their own last docs commit instead of the true fork point — verify the real fork base via `git merge-base <worktree-branch> HEAD` before recording/merging.
cargo fmt run at the crate root can reformat unrelated files as a side effect — scope-check every merge diff (`git diff --name-only <base> <branch>`) and revert stray reformats before committing.

For plans that are intentionally atomic and compile RED mid-flip, gate the merge strictly on the worktree reaching the green boundary — never merge a RED worktree, and stop-and-report rather than force it.

When repeated in-execution architectural discoveries occur (3 times in this session), stop auto-spinning re-scopes and put the decision to the user explicitly rather than silently expanding scope again.

For a migration too large for one autonomous pass with no compiling sub-unit, break it into a 'grind' of bounded slices on the same branch (each slice may leave the workspace RED by design), track carry-forward facts in a committed runbook, and gate the final merge on real end-to-end verification (not just cargo check) rather than compile-green alone.
Durable handoff scratchpad files (outside the repo) preserve full recovery state across context compaction and session/usage-limit interruptions — write/update them before any pause.

Distinguish an agent dying from an account/session usage limit (transient, retry after reset) from a genuine architectural halt with zero edits (real blocker) — the former should just be retried post-reset, not treated as a design failure.

friction: gsd-planner API crashed mid-response while writing the 14th plan, requiring manual recovery.
69-16 executor stalled mid-stream on an API error with uncommitted work, requiring manual inspection, completion of the last edit, and commit.
69-09 executor hit the account session/usage limit twice in a row before any productive work began.

Three successive architectural blockers were discovered only during execution despite full research/planning/plan-checker passes: (1) FUSE read/write path coupling, (2) missing write-plane emit API + read adapter, (3) missing write-owner tree-materialization for the read-write FUSE mount.
GSD's commit-helper false-negative on 'commit_failed' recurred on essentially every commit in the session, requiring manual git log verification each time.
A durable handoff file was initially written to a mistyped, doubled path ('phase69-phase69') and had to be moved to the correct scratchpad location.
cargo fmt crate-root reformat drift recurred across multiple executor runs (69-08, 69-15), requiring manual scope verification and reverts.
